overall_summary: The sample size is low and absolute view counts are small, but a clear pattern emerges: content focused on 'self respect' and digital/phone boundaries (chat deletion, muting chats, removing numbers) consistently outperforms abstract sadness or late-night thoughts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'चैट डिलीट करने की हिम्मत' (40 views), 'Self Respect Status Story' (39 views), and 'जब रिप्लाई का इंतज़ार खत्म हो जाए' (35 views) perform noticeably better than generic late-night or one-sided love videos.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on micro-moments involving modern smartphone habits like typing indicators, read receipts, pinning/muting chats, and contact lists.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'रात के ख्याल' and general 'ओवरथिंकिंग' without a concrete physical or digital trigger (e.g., 'मेज पर रखी चाय ठंडी हो गई') underperform, getting under 10-12 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely abstract poetic openings. Ground every emotional thought in a specific, everyday digital action.

next_video.concept: A realization that scrolling past someone's active status without clicking it anymore is the ultimate win for self-respect.
next_video.opening_direction: आज पहली बार ऐसा हुआ, जब उसका ग्रीन डॉट दिखा और अंगूठा खुद-ब-खुद स्क्रॉल कर आगे निकल गया।
next_video.twist_direction: दर्द इस बात का नहीं कि वो ऑनलाइन था, बल्कि इस बात की खुशी थी कि अब मुझे फर्क नहीं पड़ा।
next_video.reason: Aligns with the top-performing 'self-respect' category while testing a slightly different micro-action (scrolling past instead of deleting) to avoid repeating exact phrasing from past hits.

experiment: Testing active indifference (scrolling past status) versus past aggressive actions (deleting/blocking) within the self-respect theme.
